settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: CookieInterceptor is defined in struts-default.xml but I did not find it included in any default interceptor stack, so it is opt-in
isAcceptableName() restricts names to `[a-zA-Z0-9\.\]\[_'\s]+`, blocking `@`, `#`, `(`, `)`, `=`, `,` typically needed for OGNL static-method/context RCE payloads
name is matched against *name* only; the attacker-controlled portion that reaches OGNL is the cookie name restricted by the pattern
candidates.description: CookieInterceptor reads request cookies and, for names passing isAcceptableName() (the ACCEPTED_PATTERN regex `[a-zA-Z0-9\.\]\[_'\s]+`), calls stack.setValue(cookieName, cookieValue) with the raw cookie name used as an OGNL expression and the raw cookie value as the value (lines 261-288, invoked at 226-234). Cookie values are attacker-controlled and cookies are trivially set by an attacker, so both the expression (name) and the assignment value are user-influenced before reaching OGNL. The class javadoc itself notes the acceptedPattern exists "to protect against remote command execution vulnerability" (lines 202-207), which signals this path has historically been security-sensitive. Risk depends on whether the interceptor is enabled for an action (it is defined but not referenced by any default stack in struts-default.xml at the lines I inspected) and on the excluded/accepted pattern configuration.
missing_evidence: The OGNL library version and its default member-access / static-method-access behavior for this build (not visible in the reviewed source)
Whether any shipped app or default configuration enables the cookie interceptor with `*` names/values
Runtime confirmation that a value permitted by ACCEPTED_PATTERN can drive dangerous OGNL evaluation
preconditions: The `cookie` interceptor is referenced in an application action or stack configuration
cookiesName is set to `*` or to the attacker's cookie name (cookiesValue empty or `*`, or value matches cookiesValueSet)
The cookie name matches the default ACCEPTED_PATTERN and evades any OGNL safeguards in the underlying OGNL version
candidates.title: CookieInterceptor injects cookie name/value into the OGNL value stack after only a name-pattern check

counter_evidence: Hard-coded ExcludedPatterns include a class-access pattern and prefixed `struts.`, `session.`, `request.`, `application.`, `servlet(Request|Response).`, `parameters.`
ReflectionContextState.setDenyMethodExecution(contextMap, true) and setCreatingNullObjects are set on the context before setParameters (lines 241-250) and on the new stack (lines 306-308)
devMode-gated notifyDeveloper logging only affects diagnostics, not acceptance
candidates.description: ParametersInterceptor decides acceptability of each request parameter via isWithinLengthLimit(name) && !isExcluded(name) && isAccepted(name) (line 417). Exclusion is driven by hard-coded ExcludedPatterns plus any caller-supplied `excludeParams` compiled with Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE (lines 502-521). The default accepted-name pattern ACCEPTED_PARAM_NAMES (line 146) allows dot/bracket/index notation, i.e. nested OGNL property navigation, and the CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN blacklist (ExcludedPatterns line 9) is a regex whose real protection only holds if it is loaded and the value stack enforces DENY_METHOD_EXECUTION. The code sets deny-method-execution/create-null-objects flags around setParameter (lines 241-250 and 306-308), but the effective guard lives partly in the OGNL implementation and in override behavior of setExcludeParams/setAcceptParamNames by subclasses or XML configuration.
missing_evidence: The actual OGNL version/library and whether it honors DENY_METHOD_EXECUTION and blocks static method access in this build
Any application-level overrides of excludeParams/acceptParamNames that widen acceptance
End-to-end runtime proof that a name passing all three checks reaches a dangerous OGNL evaluation
preconditions: An action is reachable by untrusted HTTP requests and uses the default params stack
A parameter name evades the hard-coded/configured exclude patterns while matching the accepted pattern
The underlying OGNL/reflection layer does not independently block the navigated expression
candidates.title: ParametersInterceptor blacklist patterns are regex-configurable and the accepted-name pattern permits [] . characters

counter_evidence: The active check accepts only names in `[a-zA-Z0-9\.\]\[_'\s]+`, which excludes `@`, `#`, `(`, `)`, so the commented-out class-access check is arguably redundant given the active pattern
The interceptor is not part of any default stack I found
candidates.description: In CookieInterceptor.isAcceptableName the source contains a commented-out line that would have rejected names matching ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN, leaving only the ACCEPTED_PATTERN regex as the check (lines 247-250). This indicates the developer considered but did not apply the same class-access blacklist used by ParametersInterceptor. If ACCEPTED_PATTERN were ever relaxed or if a cookie name could contain characters that reconstruct class-access semantics, the lack of the CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN check would remove a secondary layer. This is a hardening-gap observation, not a demonstrated bypass.
missing_evidence: Whether ACCEPTED_PATTERN characters (dot, brackets, quotes) suffice for a class-access payload against the in-use OGNL version
Whether any deployment sets a custom acceptCookieNames pattern
preconditions: acceptCookieNames is overridden to a permissive pattern, or a deployment relies solely on isAcceptableName for the class-access defense
The cookie interceptor is enabled for a reachable action
candidates.title: Partial hardening for class-access exclusion is incomplete in cookie name acceptance
